timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Let's go!
Molly's Falls Pond State Park Reservoir is located just 15 miles from Montpillier
for Montpill in the rural town of Cabots.
This 411 acre pond is largely undeveloped and is an excellent spot for swimming, boating
and fishing.
Panglers confine the variety of fish including rainbow trout, brown trout, northern pipe,
paper hunt, smallmouth bass and yellow perch.
Camping in Pickney King along the shores has been a long standing tradition.
The park maintains five overnight campsites in 10 day use picnic areas all on the
water free first come first serve.
The Spruce Fur Wetland along the southern shore provides habitat to wildlife such as
mousse, deer and shoreline nesting habitat for waterfowl including this great blue heron.
Standing over 6 feet tall is the largest North American heron.
The great blue heron is found throughout most of North America as far north as Alaska in the summer.
And in the winter the range extends as far south as Florida, Mexico and the Caribbean.
The primary food for great blue heron is small fish.
Though it is also known to opportunistically feed on a wide range of other small prey like
the crayfish found in Molleuse Falls pond.
The northern of bluets is a newcomer to Vermont with its first sighting in 2016.
These damselflies inhabit fresh water bodies across North America.
Their larvae start out in the water and look more like a crustacean.
But after several mulls, wings emerge and become the adults gracing ponds, lakes, streams and marshes
with their brilliant blue vestments.
The common loom has also been on the pond for a number of years.
This stealthy divers submerges without making a splash to catch fish.
The common loom produces a variety of distinctive and often haunting vocalizations.
The most common of which are the tremolo, the yodel, the whale and the hoot.
Each of these calls communicates a distinctive message.
Under the pond we find pumpkin seed, perch, trout, pickerel, bass and evenis catfish.
During the summer the reservoir bustles with people enjoying water sports, fishing and boating.
